newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs to launch stock market in Sept - official.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs to launch stock market in Sept - official.

text.p: Kazakhstan's stock market will be launched in September, and portfolio investors are expected to inject around $200 million into Kazakh corporate securities by the end of this year, a senior official announced on Wednesday.
"We will start deals on the stock exchange in September," Grigory Marchenko, Chairman of the National Securities Commission, told Reuters.
The launch of the stock market -- initially scheduled for May or June -- has been put off several times.
"It is unrealistic to expect that we can create a fully-fledged stock market in a few months after five years of talks," Marchenko said.
"But the most important (factor) in building a stock market is to have a political will, and Kazakhstan has it."
"The legal framework is some 70 percent ready, and now the most important thing is to adopt a new law on joint-stock companies," he said.

The government of the resource-rich Central Asian state -- five times the size of France and with a population of just 16.7 million people -- has selected 13 large Kazakh companies, whose stakes would be offered first to portfolio investors.
The 13 firms are part of around 60 companies designated by the government to become "blue chips" and the core of the future stock market.

"We expect that investors will pay at least $80 million to buy stakes in these first 13 companies...The total level of investment in Kazakh corporate securities may reach $200 million by the end of this year," Marchenko said.
In line with a government decision, state-owned shares in nine companies will be sold to investors directly on the stock exchange through local broker and dealer companies.
These nine companies will offer to investors stakes of three to 39 percent.

The companies include AO Alyuminii Kazakhstana alumina works, AO Kazkhrom chrome producer, titanium-magnesium producer AO Ust-Kamenogorsky Titano-Magniyevy Kombinat, lead producer AO Shymkentsky Svintsovy Zavod and state-run Halyk Savings Bank.

Stakes in the remaining four companies would be offered to portfolio investors through large foreign investment institutions, and eight foreign banks are vying for the right to work with these companies.

Investors will be offered five-percent stakes in Zhezkazgantsvetmet copper producer and the Mangistaumunaigaz and Aktobemunaigaz oil companies. They will also be offered a 4.5-percent stake in the Kazakhtelekom telecoms monopoly.
Marchenko said the second, and final, round of the tender to select four investment banks would be over by August 15.
He said strategic investors, already holding large or majority stakes in the 13 companies, would not be barred from increasing their stakes by buying shares on the stock market.
